clue.text: See Englishman about cuts

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: to see is to spot
POM is Australian slang for an Englishman

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and visit an Englishman regarding some cuts, perhaps budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SPOTPOM backwards. 'cuts' means haircuts here, not reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Mop-tops are shaggy, fringed haircuts of the kind the early Beatles wore, so they are cuts of hair.

clue.text: Result of using tight controls on Middle Eastern leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, so the opening letter of each of the seven words is taken

explanation.surface: A political commentary on what happens when strict controls are imposed on rulers in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The leaders are the first letters of 'of using tight controls on Middle Eastern', not the political leaders the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end product of something, which is what a result is.

clue.text: State half-time wager

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters, the front half of time

parts.note: a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: Someone placing a bet at half-time in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first half of 'time', giving TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a region of China once regarded as an independent country, so a state in the sense of a nation.

clue.text: Dish including T-bone

indicators.note: including means one thing holds another within it, so the letter goes inside the dish

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish
the T of T-bone, taken as the letter itself

explanation.surface: A dish served with a T-bone steak in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T-bone' splits: the T is the inserted letter and 'bone' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a small bone at the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Easy on Prince Andrew?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for something easily done
Prince Andrew claimed in a 2019 TV interview that he could not sweat

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside suggesting something comes easily to Prince Andrew.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Andrew, in a 2019 BBC interview, said a medical condition left him unable to sweat; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is no sweat means it causes no trouble, so it is easy.

clue.text: Single, appearing for the first time, extremely arty, after love …

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the zero in the answer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O
something appearing for the first time is new

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A description of someone single, a debutant with a very arty look, following a lost love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the ends of 'arty', AY. 'Single' refers to a ticket, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A single ticket is a one-way ticket, valid for the outward journey only.

clue.text: … and portrayed as shy

parts.note: and can mean with, as in 'fish and chips' or 'fish with chips'
something portrayed in a picture has been drawn

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue's single person, now depicted as timid.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 6 down; the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawn person is reserved and keeps to themselves, much like someone shy.

clue.text: Purity of peas cultivated by relative

indicators.note: cultivated land is worked over, so the letters of peas are turned over into a new order

parts.note: sis, short for sister, is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative growing peas of very high quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges PEAS into ASEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Asepsis is the absence of harmful germs, a sterile cleanliness or purity.

clue.text: Disease from Eastbourne, say

parts.note: read the answer itself as a set of instructions: its second word, split in two, tells you to put its first word's letters in a new order, and the result is this word

explanation.surface: A worry about illness coming out of a south-coast English town.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split RESORT as RE-SORT, an instruction to rearrange SEASIDE, which gives DISEASE. Eastbourne is a seaside town in Sussex, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastbourne is an example of a coastal holiday town, which the 'say' signals.

clue.text: Tone from this straight trip

definitions.meaning: in music, going from A up to B is an interval of a whole tone
an ... journey goes directly from start to finish

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about sounding off from a direct journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical note A to the note B is a whole tone; 'A to B' also means a simple direct journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole tone in music spans two semitones, the step between notes A and B; a direct route is from point A to point B.

clue.text: 1 getting Tesla — bet he crashes!

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 1 across, the haircuts this band made famous

indicators.note: a car that crashes is smashed up, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone buying a Tesla car while a friend wagers it will crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashes' rearranges TESLA BET HE. The definition '1' points to the haircuts at 1 across: the band is the one known for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles were famous for their mop-top haircuts, so the cross-reference stands for the group by association.

clue.text: Human ethical argument finally accepted

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: ethical means moral

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of argument

explanation.surface: A philosophical point that a moral argument was eventually accepted by people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T, the end of 'argument', which 'accepted' puts inside MORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal is a being who must die, that is a person rather than a god.

clue.text: Careless hit and run

parts.note: to slap is to hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A reckless hit-and-run driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and without proper attention.

clue.text: Spooner gets B, D#, F# permutations from these instruments

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of two words, so the two pieces trade their first consonant sounds

parts.note: the letter B is said as 'bee'
the notes B, D sharp and F sharp in any arrangement make B major chords

explanation.surface: A musical exercise in arranging the notes of a B major chord.
explanation.walkthrough: B, D# and F# are the notes of B major, so their permutations are 'B chords'; swapping the opening sounds of 'bee chords' gives 'key boards'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyboards are instruments played with keys, such as pianos and synthesisers.

clue.text: Prohibit a clone being developed in this city

parts.note: to bar something is to prohibit it

indicators.note: something being developed is changing form, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A call to ban human cloning research in some city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being developed' rearranges CLONE into CELON; the A stays put at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the Catalan capital in north-east Spain, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Endless Jesus raps from the east? Take a break

indicators.note: in an across answer, reading from the east means right to left, so the letters run backwards
endless means each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A weary listener wanting a break from endless religious rapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' strips both words to ESU and AP; 'from the east' reads ESUAP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause is to stop briefly, which is to take a break.

clue.text: Gem that's mostly white or pink with green sides

definitions.text: Gem that's mostly white or pink

parts.note: pea green is a shade of green
R and L stand for right and left, the two sides

explanation.surface: A description of a gemstone's colours: pale body, green edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs long: pearls are usually white or pinkish. 'sides' gives R and L, for right and left.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a lustrous gem formed inside an oyster, typically white, cream or rosy in colour.

clue.text: What about mine? A quiet final tribute

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the questioning word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?
a pit is a coal mine
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A miner asking about their own memorial, a quiet last farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' is the questioning EH, not a question word in the clue's sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is an inscription on a gravestone, a last tribute to the dead.

clue.text: Senior officers kiss cheek

parts.note: the brass, or top brass, are senior military officers
to neck is to kiss

explanation.surface: High-ranking officers giving a kiss on the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass neck is British slang for brazen nerve or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek in the sense of impudent boldness is what brass neck means.

clue.text: Boot wearer, upset about closure, takes off

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed cat goes around the other word
upset in a down answer means turned upside down, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: Puss in Boots is the fairy-tale cat
a closure is an end

explanation.surface: Someone in boots, upset that something is closing, storms off.
explanation.walkthrough: Puss in Boots is the fairy-tale cat; in a down answer 'upset' turns its name over. 'takes off' means mimics, not departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is to mimic or parody, the same as to take off someone.

clue.text: Work ethics to welcome mathematical chief boffin

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one letter is placed inside the other letters
to work something is to knead or reshape it, so the letters are reworked
the chief letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: A research rule about ethics welcoming a lead mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' rearranges ETHICS to CHEIST; 'to welcome' puts the M from 'chief' of 'mathematical' inside it. Boffin is British slang for a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist is a scientist, and a boffin is informal British for a scientist or expert.

clue.text: Get the better of idiot joining higher education establishment

parts.note: the OU is the Open University, a British distance-learning university
a twit is an idiot

explanation.surface: A fool enrolling at a university to improve themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University (OU) is a UK university teaching mainly by distance learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone is to beat them through cleverness.

clue.text: Starting with impenetrable vacant stare, reported appearance of US Mafiosi

indicators.note: starting picks the opening letters, here of the two words with and impenetrable
a vacant word is emptied of its middle, leaving its first and last letters
reported means spoken aloud, so the answer sounds like the word given

parts.note: a guise is an outward appearance

explanation.surface: A description of a mobster's impenetrable blank stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting' takes WI; 'vacant' empties 'stare' to SE; 'reported' gives a word sounding like GUISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiseguys is American slang for members of the Mafia.

clue.text: Sounds coming from reactionary and half-hearted session

indicators.note: a reactionary wants to go back, so the word runs backwards
half of the double S at the heart of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Noises made in an uninspired session by a reactionary group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of SESSION's central SS, giving SESION; 'reactionary' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises are sounds, especially loud or unwanted ones.

clue.text: Matilda's mature figure

parts.note: Matilda is the setter, so Matilda's means the setter is: I'm
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: The setter boasting of their grown-up figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Matilda is this puzzle's setter, so 'Matilda's' stands for I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a figure in the sense of a representation or likeness.

clue.text: Best not to open this farm — no cows unfortunately!

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Advice not to start a farm if there are no cows for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges FARM NO COWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A can of worms is a situation full of trouble, which one is wise not to open.

clue.text: Some monosaccharides get desiccated

indicators.note: some means a part of the word, so the answer lies within it

explanation.surface: Some sugars dry out.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means extremely dry, as does desiccated.

clue.text: Prevents tooth enamel defects

indicators.note: enamel is the outer coating of a tooth, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: warts are blemishes or defects, as in 'warts and all'

explanation.surface: A dental product that stops flaws in tooth enamel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enamel' coats the outside of 'tooth', giving its outer letters TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart is to stop or frustrate, so thwarts means prevents.

clue.text: Abundantly rocky planet, last in galaxy

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order
last in picks the final letter of the word galaxy

explanation.surface: A rocky planet lying plentifully at the edge of a galaxy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges PLANET into APLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplenty means in abundance, as in 'food aplenty', an adverb like abundantly.
